answer: Each identity docks at a jetty and posts a $90 premium into a mutual cover orchard of 20 members. Five rotating auditors check one random member of each orchard every epoch, and a proven fake burns the whole orchard cover, wiping every premium inside. The forfeit then climbs terrace tiers with the size of the fraud cluster, so one fake loses $180, ten fakes lose $990 each, and a hundred fakes lose $9,090 each. One honest agent risks $90, but 100 clones lose $9,090 each, $909,000 in all, 10,100 times the honest price. Tending one orchard is cheap; a forest of fakes bankrupts its planter.
